chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd al-Aḥwaṣ al-Qummī narrated to me, saying:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: How many rakʿahs is the salat (prayer)? He said: “Fifty-one rakʿahs.”
In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.
And to Him belongs all praise, and through Him we seek help.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the salat (prayer), referring here to the total daily prescribed and recommended prayer units
key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: praise, ascribed entirely to Allah in the closing formula
key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: a rakʿah, one unit of ritual prayer
key_terms.لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the Imam being addressed in the narration
key_terms.نَسْتَعِينُ: we seek help, indicating reliance upon Allah

ai.seo_question: How many total daily rakʿahs of salat (prayer) are reported from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports from al-Riḍā عليه السلام that the total number of daily salat (prayer) units is fifty-one rakʿahs. It is significant in the context of the prescribed and recommended prayers, especially in Shia fiqh concerning the daily nawāfil alongside the obligatory prayers.
